newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine funds dominated by three banks - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentine funds dominated by three banks - report.

text.p: Three financial institutions hold more than 50 percent of the assets invested in Argentina's fast-growing mutual funds industry, according to a report acquired by Reuters on Tuesday.
The report, prepared by the Argentine Chamber of Mutual Funds, said $1.71 billion of assets were controlled by three institutions, out of a total $3.30 billion.
Boston Asset Management SA, controlled by Bank of Boston Corp, headed the list with assets worth $844 million, or 25.6 percent of the total.
Pecuaria SA, owned by Banco Frances, was second, with $458.8 million in assets. Geinver Gerente SA, controlled by Banco Rio, came in third with $410 million.
Argentina's mutual funds were set up in the 1960s but strong growth only began last year. In 1990 they managed just $40 million in assets.
So far in 1997 their assets have risen 77 percent. There are some 168 funds in the market, which are run by 61 financial institutions.

Asked about the concentration of funds, Fabian Ciarlotti, market manager at Schroders Mildesa Investment Management SA, said: "The mutual fund industry is in a stage of birth and in a strong growth process...There is concentration, but so far there are no real comparisons since we will have to look at the market in four, five or six years."
